meta.title: Tri-alliance clash — Kingshot 777
meta.description: Beginner-friendly guide to Kingshot Tri-Alliance Clash: the monthly cycle, entry requirements, energy, squad setup, scoring, phases, the 30-player role split and the temple endgame.

tldr.heading: TL;DR
items: Three alliances, 60 minutes, every four weeks. Points come from holding buildings, and the winner is usually whoever holds the temple at the end.
The Temple of Tides opens at minute 40. First capture pays a one-off 50,000 points, then 1,800 points per minute while you hold it. Everything before phase 4 is setup for that fight.
Energy is your real limit. Moving, capturing, charging, retreating, reviving and conscripting all cost it. Arrive at minute 20 and minute 40 with a reserve.
Stay in your lane. Six lanes, one main player each. A collapsed lane is a hole in your map for the rest of the event.
Two supporters keep each main player alive. They rotate forward while the main player heals, so nobody eats the 2-minute respawn walk from HQ.
Five squads to skip a building. That's why the special force of six players (18 squads) can drive straight through enemy territory.
The special force never splits. It exists to break through and cause chaos, not to win duels.
Don't overextend. Push only as fast as your supporters can follow, and stay near your anchor building.

firstClash.heading: If this is your first clash
items: Get registered. Tell your R4/R5 you want in during the sign-up window. You cannot register yourself.
Set up your three squad presets before you enter. You can't calmly rebuild marches once the clock is running.
Learn your lane and role in the 3-minute prep phase. Ask which building is yours and who your supporters are.
Take your assigned building as soon as the phase opens. Don't improvise.
Stay in your lane. A lane that empties is a hole for the rest of the hour.
Don't chase kills. Kills score nothing directly. Buildings and time do.
Save energy for minute 20 and minute 40. Those are the two moments the match is actually decided.

scoring.heading: What actually scores

rows.points: 50,000 one-off for the first capture, then 1,800 per minute held

items: The 50,000 is for capturing the Temple first, not for holding it at the whistle. If another alliance caps it before you, the match is not over — retaking and holding still pays 1,800 per minute, and twenty minutes of that outweighs the bonus.
Kills only matter as a means. You kill to open a building or to keep one. Killing for its own sake spends energy and buys nothing.

energy.heading: Energy
energy.body: This is the mechanic beginners lose to most often. Energy is spent on moving, capturing, charging, retreating, reviving and conscripting. Run out and you cannot answer the Garrison or Temple call, no matter how strong your account is.
items: Don't burn energy chasing kills in the first 20 minutes. Aim to still have a healthy reserve at minute 20, and again at minute 40.
Assign a Captain after capturing a point. It improves energy recovery, which is one reason having R4+ players on the field helps.
Retreat one building back to heal and conscript out of combat. That's cheaper than instant revive, and far cheaper than dying and eating the ~2-minute walk from HQ.
Leaving the battlefield has a re-entry cooldown — commonly cited as around 12 minutes. Most account buffs still apply on the field, except some march speed and capacity effects.

squadSetup.heading: Squad setup
squadSetup.intro: You field three marches, so nine heroes are in rotation. Build the three as presets before you enter:
presets: Squad 1 — strongest combat squad. For high-pressure buildings and contested caps.
Squad 2 — stable squad. Lane support and reinforcement; it has to survive, not spike.
Squad 3 — flexible squad. Routes, recovery cover, retakes.
items: Don't even the three out just to make the power numbers look balanced. Each squad needs a job; three identical mediocre marches do none of them well.
There is no universal formation ratio. It depends on your troops, your heroes, the opponent, and whether you're attacking or holding.
Consider holding one strong march back for the minute-20 Garrison and minute-40 Temple timings.

eventFormat.heading: Event format
items: Soldier power is not used for matchmaking. You can be paired against far stronger alliances, so structure and discipline are what you control.
You cannot leave the alliance once you've entered the battlefield.

rows.matters:
R4/R5 place marks on the map.
Everyone confirms their lane and role.

Garrisons are shielded and cannot be touched.
Main players take their lane keypoint fast,
supporters settle into the building behind it,
reaction teams sweep the neutral buildings in the centre.
Secure the Transit Hubs and route buildings you'll need later.

A24, B24 and C24 unlock and pay 1,800 per minute.
Priority 1 is holding your own garrison; priority 2 is taking an enemy one.
Start the regroup toward the Temple before minute 40, not at it.
The special force is at its most active here.

Attack the Temple of Tides in one coordinated burst, not one march at a time.
Defend the access routes around A29, B29 and C29.
This phase decides the match.

rows.job: One per lane. Capture the lane keypoint immediately, then hold the frontline and keep the enemy out of your interior.
Two per main player. Sit in the building behind the keypoint, step forward only when your main player needs to heal, and never leave the keypoint unmanned.
A single breakthrough group. Skips low-value buildings, takes undefended structures deep in enemy territory, and forces enemy rotations.
Grab the central neutral buildings at the start, then float: retake lost buildings and prop up whichever lane is under pressure.
Buff management only. No lane fighting.

qa.q: Why does the special force work?
qa.a: Bypassing a building without capturing it needs five squads. Six players fielding three squads each is 18 squads, enough to skip repeatedly and cover ground fast. Split the group and it stops working — nobody has five squads on their own.

Smaller, highly active players who can stay focused for the full 60 minutes. Buff timing swings lane fights and the temple battle, so this is a real job, not a place to park someone weak and inattentive.

map.heading: The map
map.body: Six lanes feed one centre. Lanes 1, 4 and 5 sit in the upper half, lanes 2, 3 and 6 in the lower half; the garrisons and the temple approaches are the only objectives that decide the score.

healingRotation.heading: Healing rotation
healingRotation.body: This is the mechanic that separates an organised alliance from a mob. When a main player gets low:
steps: One supporter advances and takes over the frontline.
The main player pulls back briefly to heal.
The main player returns as soon as they're healed.
The supporter falls back to the anchor building behind the keypoint.
healingRotation.outro: The lane never goes quiet, the keypoint is never empty, and nobody has to walk two minutes back from HQ after dying.

commonMistakes.heading: Common mistakes
items: Overextending. Deep solo pushes leave you cut off from your supporters and hand the enemy free kills.
Splitting the special force. Below five squads it can't skip buildings, and its whole value disappears.
Supporters pushing ahead. Their strength is stability. An aggressive supporter is a keypoint about to be lost.
Reaction teams rotating for no reason. They should move when a lane is genuinely in trouble, not chase every skirmish.
Rotating to the temple too late. Lanes need to converge together; arriving piecemeal means being beaten piecemeal.

qa.q: I'm new — what's the one thing I should get right?
qa.a: Stay in your lane and save energy. Everything else your R4s can work around; those two they can't.
Only as a means to hold a building or to open one. There are no points for kills themselves, and duels you didn't need cost energy you'll want at minute 40.

qa.q: What if the enemy caps the Temple first?
qa.a: Retake it. They get the one-off 50,000, but the 1,800 per minute is still live for whoever holds it — and there are up to twenty minutes of that on the table.
Usually no. Retreat one building back, heal and conscript out of combat. Instant revive burns energy you'll need for the next call.
Strongly recommended. The minute-20 garrison call and the minute-40 temple push happen far too fast to coordinate over text.

healingRotation.title: The four-step healing rotation
healingRotation.caption: The rotation runs clockwise and repeats; the frontline is always occupied.
